name: Anterior spinocerebellar tract
modality: proprioceptive and interneuronal feedback from the lower limb
summary: Neurons at the base of the dorsal horn and in the intermediate gray of the lumbosacral cord send axons that mostly cross in the anterior white commissure, ascend in the anterolateral funiculus in front of the posterior spinocerebellar tract, pass through the medulla and pons, and enter the cerebellum through the superior cerebellar peduncle, where most cross back so that each side of the cerebellum still receives information from its own side of the body. It carries less pure proprioception and more information about the activity of spinal interneurons, telling the cerebellum what the spinal circuits are doing with the descending commands.

origin.note: Spinal border cells and intermediate gray of the lumbosacral segments; input from Golgi tendon organs, flexor reflex afferents and descending tracts.

neuronChain.synapse: cerebellar cortex of the anterior lobe (vermis and paravermis) via the superior cerebellar peduncle, crossing twice

decussation.level: Anterior white commissure (crosses) and superior cerebellar peduncle (crosses back)
decussation.note: Double crossing makes the net projection ipsilateral.

waypoints.note: anterolateral funiculus, anterior to the posterior spinocerebellar tract
enters through the superior peduncle at the upper pons

termination: Cerebellar anterior lobe vermis and intermediate zone, ipsilateral to the origin after the second crossing.

lesionEffectsByLevel.effects: Ipsilateral leg ataxia (net effect after double crossing), usually mixed with spinothalamic signs
Ataxia with the cerebellar outflow signs dominating

pearls: This is the only spinocerebellar tract that enters through the superior peduncle
It monitors spinal interneurons rather than joints: a copy of what the cord is doing
